answer: This week's school newsletter, the newest notice: 'The concert time has changed. It now starts at 6 pm.'
A poster the school put up last month, before the change: 'The concert starts at 5 pm.'
A text Mo's cousin sent last month. He isn't at the school. 'I think it's at 7.'
alsoDefensible: Poster and text could be swapped: the poster is out of date (superseded by the change), so a child could argue it is as unreliable as the guess. But the poster comes from the school and was once accurate, while the cousin is not at the school and only guesses, so poster above text.
note: Newsletter first is certain; the order of the last two rests on 'who made it' (school vs outsider) outweighing 'when'.
